answer: Funding-source throttling resists Sybil attacks: the network traces each new identity's first deposit back to its funding source, and the creation fee and waiting period spiral upward with every additional identity from the same source. Honest users creating one identity pay almost nothing, while an attacker funding a thousand fakes faces a river of rising costs that quickly exceeds any gain. The bridge between a wallet and its identities is public, so splitting funds across fresh wallets only adds its own transfer costs and leaves a traceable pattern.
